rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code; distinguish supplied evidence from inference.
rules.rationale: Project-wide meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes a factual change.

rules.intent: Set the intended audience and prerequisites; explain required terms rather than replacing every technical word. Fit the causal links and any relevant prediction into the requested answer format.
rules.rationale: Modern audience-specific adaptation; no universal age target.
exceptions: Use the audience specified by the user; ask only when the missing prerequisite changes the explanation.

rules.intent: Explain how the parts produce the result; identify missing links and verify them with relevant evidence before revising.
rules.rationale: Adapts explanation as a diagnostic of understanding, without an authentic historical algorithm claim.
exceptions: If evidence is unavailable, retain a precise unresolved question rather than inventing a causal link.

rules.intent: Use examples or analogies only with their relevant correspondence and limits; retain conditions and uncertainty.
rules.rationale: Project adaptation for technically faithful explanation.
exceptions: A literal mechanism may be clearer than an analogy.

rules.intent: Check the explanation with a new application or counterexample; distinguish a proposed test from demonstrated mastery.
rules.rationale: Operational adaptation of the warning that explanation alone does not establish problem-solving ability.
exceptions: Do not force an interactive quiz when the user requested a finished explanation; include a worked transfer example instead.
